name: ECCC Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations Reported Data: combined sewer overflow points (annual)
waters_covered: every WSER-reporting system with combined sewers (6,881 rows; Quebec 5,854, Ontario 498, NB 170, BC 55, MB 36)
access_detail: CSV via https://data-donnees.az.ec.gc.ca/api/file?path=%2Fsubstances%2Fplaninfrastruture%2Fwastewater-systems-effluent-regulations-reported-data%2FResaeu-Wser-unitaires-combined-points.csv (302 to a signed blob; cp1252 encoding). Companion files: Resaeu-Wser-identification.csv, Resaeu-Wser-surveillance-monitoring.csv. Border extract research/border/raw/eccc-wser-cso-points-border-2024.json; sample eccc-wser-combined-points-sample.csv.
fields: Number of CSO points that discharged during the year
legal_basis: Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations, SOR/2012-139 (Fisheries Act)
status_reason: The only Canada-wide overflow record: per wastewater system and year, how many CSO points discharged and how many exist, with the system's lat/lon. Annual only; no dates, volumes or outfall points.
notes: Annual totals only; good for the 'annual totals' grade and to name upstream systems. 'No Data / Pas de données' in 1,501 rows.

name: ECCC WSER identification and effluent monitoring files
status_reason: System identity and effluent quality; not overflow events.

name: Statistics Canada combined sewer overflow discharge volumes (by month, province and drainage region)
status_reason: Aggregated by drainage region; no system or event detail.

name: Natural Resources Canada National Hydro Network (NHN) and Canadian Hydrospatial Network (CHN)
status_reason: Replaces NHD north of the border for reach tracing and water names (NHD stops at the border; NHDPlus HR includes some cross-border catchments, unverified). OpenStreetMap waterways are the fallback for names.

name: International Joint Commission (Great Lakes Water Quality Agreement; boundary waters boards)
status_reason: Policy and science reports on transboundary sewage (Detroit River, Lake Erie, Lake of the Woods, Souris, Red); no event data.

name: Ontario CLI-ECA (Consolidated Linear Infrastructure Environmental Compliance Approval) Schedule E: bypass and overflow reporting
operator: Ontario Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks (MECP)
legal_basis: Ontario Water Resources Act s.53; Environmental Protection Act; CLI-ECA Schedule E
status_reason: Reporting is to MECP's Spills Action Centre, the medical officer of health and downstream users, plus annual public performance reports and CSO signage; real-time public notice is not a general duty (a 2022 public comment asked for it). Condition text not read.
notes: Municipal CLI-ECA annual reports (for example Leamington 2025, St. Catharines 2024) are public PDFs listing each bypass and overflow: annual, dated.

name: MECP online reporting tool for municipal bypasses and overflows (ERO 019-5378, 2022)
status_reason: Voluntary reporting tool expanded to all municipalities in 2022; no public output found (data.ontario.ca search for overflow/bypass: 0 results).

name: City of Windsor 'Bypass Events' open data (bypass_events.csv)
access_detail: Two columns, ISO local times; 63 rows, 2024-08-01 to 2026-09-03. Catalogue page https://opendata.citywindsor.ca/Details/242 says the catalogue has moved to a new portal; the old file still updated 2026-11-03. Sample research/border/raw/windsor-bypass-events-sample.csv.
cadence: checked every 48 hours, file regenerated every 24 hours
license: City of Windsor open data licence (not read)
status_reason: A machine-readable, dated record of treatment-plant bypasses into the Detroit River, refreshed every 24 hours; start and end only.
notes: Description: 'A bypass event occurs when flow monitors register any volume (cubic metres/day) above 0. The end of the bypass event occurs when the value returns back to 0.' Windsor's CSOs (26 points in WSER) are not in this file.

name: Utilities Kingston real-time sewer overflow map and overflow log
waters_covered: Great Cataraqui River, Little Cataraqui Creek, Kingston waterfront (Lake Ontario, St. Lawrence)
access_detail: https://utilitieskingston.com/overflows and https://utilitieskingston.com/Wastewater/SewerOverflow/Log both 403 behind a JavaScript challenge.
status_reason: Ontario's model real-time overflow map (since 2017) on Lake Ontario at the head of the St. Lawrence (shared with New York, a live state), with a log back to 2000; Cloudflare challenge (HTTP 403 'Just a moment...') to both curl and WebFetch.
notes: Utility advice (news): consider overflow information 'for at least 48 hours after a sewer overflow has occurred'. Ask Utilities Kingston for a data feed or permission.

name: City of Toronto Beaches Water Quality open data (E. coli, daily in season)
status_reason: Daily summer E. coli results and swim status for Toronto beaches on Lake Ontario, CKAN API, open licence.
notes: Toronto publishes no bypass or CSO event dataset (CKAN search 'bypass OR overflow sewage': nothing relevant), despite a 2015 ministry decision under the Environmental Bill of Rights that it report bypasses to the public in real time. Ashbridges Bay alone reported 195 of 271 CSO points discharging in 2024 (WSER).

name: Niagara Region open data: Combined Sewage Overflow (from the Monthly Bypass Incident Reporting Program)
status_reason: Yearly CSO and bypass files (2014 onward) for systems on the Niagara River, Welland Canal, Lake Ontario and Lake Erie (shared with New York); the portal returned HTTP 403 to curl and WebFetch.
notes: Search snippets describe yearly resources such as 'Combined Sewage Overflow (CSO) 2020'. Precision unknown (monthly program).

name: Ontario municipal CLI-ECA annual sewage collection reports (Sarnia, Windsor, Fort Erie, Niagara Falls, St. Catharines, Cornwall, Fort Frances, Sault Ste. Marie, Thunder Bay ...)
status_reason: Annual PDFs that list each bypass and overflow with dates and volumes; dated but a year late.

name: Swim Guide (Swim Drink Fish): Ontario beach status
status_reason: Aggregates Ontario health-unit beach results; prior art.

name: MELCCFP 'Ouvrages de surverse - Débordements d'eaux usées' (SOMAEU annual indicators per overflow structure)
operator: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
waters_covered: all Quebec municipal overflow structures (32,731 rows, 2017 to 2023)
access_detail: CSV https://www.donneesquebec.ca/recherche/dataset/64372248-d60b-4a2b-a326-bf34c721e568/resource/54190fb7-df03-4a56-b6f3-3059c0b8f1fd/download/ouvrages-de-surverse-debordements-2024-10-11.csv (12 MB, comma-delimited, UTF-8). Metadata PDF dated 2026-08-18. Atlas de l'eau web map. Sample research/border/raw/quebec-os-debordements-sample.csv.
legal_basis: Règlement sur les ouvrages municipaux d'assainissement des eaux usées (ROMAEU), RLRQ c. Q-2, r. 34.1
status_reason: Every Quebec overflow structure with outfall coordinates and yearly counts and durations by context (dry weather, rain/melt, emergency, works); CC-BY 4.0. Covers Lake Memphremagog (Magog), Missisquoi Bay tributaries (Bedford, Frelighsburg, Sutton) and the St. John headwaters (Dégelis, Pohénégamook).
notes: Overflows under 12 minutes are not counted (metadata). LIEN_SOMM_DEBRD links each structure-year to a monthly summary PDF (see xb-qc-somaeu-summary).

name: MELCCFP SOMAEU 'Synthèse des débordements' per overflow structure (monthly counts and durations, PDF)
access_detail: Parameters NO_MEF_LIEU (plant), ID_OS (structure), ANNEE, TypeDoc=SOMMAIRE_DEBORDEMENT. 2026 returns a 302 JSON (not yet available). Sample research/border/raw/quebec-somaeu-sommaire-lacolle-richelieu-2022.txt.
fills_event_fields: month (count and total duration per month, by regulatory and supplementary norm)
cadence: annual, about three months after year end
license: not stated on the PDF (dataset is CC-BY 4.0)
status_reason: Monthly precision per structure, already available for 2025 (produced 2026-03-26), ahead of the open-data CSV; text PDF, one request per structure and year.
notes: This is the 'monthly' grade: month-precision reports get the monthly mark, never red or yellow.

name: Ville de Montréal 'Débordements' (daily overflow durations per structure)
status_reason: Daily precision, but Montreal's outfalls are downstream of every shared water (the St. Lawrence below the New York border); out of scope by the owner's rule. Model of what SOMAEU data can look like.

name: Richelieu River overflows (Lacolle, Saint-Jean-sur-Richelieu)
status_reason: The Richelieu drains Lake Champlain northward; Quebec outfalls on it are downstream of Vermont and New York and do not affect US water. (Missisquoi Bay tributaries do.)

name: St. Stephen, NB (St. Croix River, opposite Calais, Maine): WSER CSO points
status_reason: WSER shows 11 of 13 CSO points discharged in 2024 into the shared St. Croix; no provincial or town event feed found (not searched in depth). Maine is a live state.
notes: From xb-ca-eccc-wser-cso. Edmundston (Saint John River boundary reach, opposite Madawaska, ME) not found in the WSER CSO file; not searched further.

name: City of Winnipeg combined sewer overflow real-time map (Red and Assiniboine rivers)
status_reason: The Red River flows north out of the US; Winnipeg's CSOs do not reach any US water. Out of scope by the owner's rule.

name: Metro Vancouver real-time sewer overflow map (last 48 hours)
status_reason: Near-real-time overflows from Metro Vancouver's system; receiving waters are the Fraser (not shared), Burrard Inlet and English Bay, which connect to the Salish Sea only at a distance. Map viewer https://gis.metrovancouver.org/mvmaps/sewer not probed.

name: Capital Regional District (Victoria) wastewater overflow notices for Greater Victoria shorelines
status_reason: Storm overflow advisories along Juan de Fuca and Haro Strait shorelines (shared Salish Sea with Washington), signs until enterococci fall below 70 CFU/100 mL; reach the public through news. CRD feed not located.

name: BC dischargers upstream of Washington, Idaho and Montana (Columbia at Trail/Castlegar, Okanagan at Osoyoos/Oliver, Elk River into Lake Koocanusa)
status_reason: Shared waters flowing into the US; no public overflow feed found (not searched in depth). WSER annual CSO file has only 55 BC rows.

name: San Diego Regional Water Quality Control Board: 'USIBWC Spill Events and Transboundary Flow Events from Mexico into the San Diego Region'
operator: California Regional Water Quality Control Board, San Diego Region
waters_covered: Tijuana River, canyon collectors (Stewart's Drain, Smuggler's Gulch, Goat Canyon, Canyon del Sol ...), Pacific shoreline
access_detail: HTML table; curl gets an Incapsula block ('Request unsuccessful'), WebFetch reads it. Updated about weekly 'if needed'; page last updated 2026-05-27 (newest row 2026-03-14 when checked).

sample_record.Event Type: Dry Weather Canyon Collector Transboundary Flow Event
sample_record.Notes: Transboundary flows were caused by an outage at PB-1 in Mexico, upstream of Stewart's Drain.

cadence: USIBWC preliminary reports 'within three days of the event'; monthly river-flow reports; table updated about weekly
license: California state web content; not stated
legal_basis: Order No. R9-2021-0001 as amended, NPDES CA0108928 (USIBWC South Bay International WWTP)
status_reason: The dated public record of Mexican sewage reaching California (Tijuana River, Stewart's Drain, Smuggler's Gulch and other canyon collectors): start, end, type, location, volume, recovered volume, notes; since 2023.
notes: A 'Tijuana River Transboundary Flow Event' starting 2023-10-11 is listed as ongoing: the river carries sewage continuously, which is a standing condition, not an event.

name: USIBWC press releases on transboundary flows (WordPress media library)
operator: U.S. Section, International Boundary and Water Commission
status_reason: Dated PDF releases on Tijuana River, Stewart's Drain and Nogales flows, discoverable as JSON (22 matching 'transboundary flow', 2025-04 to 2026-08).
notes: E.g. 'Transboundary Flow Caused By Thunderstorms 08-07-26', 'Transboundary Flow at Stewart's Drain 03-17-26'.

name: USIBWC spill notification email list (Binational Tijuana River Spill Notification Protocol)
status_reason: The protocol says USIBWC 'will immediately notify U.S. recipients of USIBWC email list serve developed for these cases' when CESPT reports a pump or pipeline failure; sign-up route not published (owner to request).
notes: CESPT notifies the Mexican Section 'within the hour, whenever this is possible'; information: cause, location, start date and time, volume, actions, expected repair time. Nogales has a similar protocol since 2022 (OOMAPAS to Mexican Section to USIBWC; IBWC roundtable 2026-08-20).

name: USIBWC Water Data Portal (Tijuana River at the international boundary and other gauges)
status_reason: Flow at the boundary shows when the river is carrying sewage across; context, not reports.

name: Arizona DEQ water quality alerts for Nogales Wash and Potrero Creek (Mexican sewage overflows)
status_reason: ADEQ press releases advise avoiding contact with Nogales Wash during cross-border SSOs; occasional.

name: Comisión Estatal de Servicios Públicos de Tijuana (CESPT) notices
status_reason: Source of the Tijuana spills; notifies CILA under the protocol; public channel (social accounts) not searched.

name: CONAGUA (Comisión Nacional del Agua): national water-quality monitoring network and discharge permits
status_reason: No public sewage spill feed known; the monitoring network publishes periodic water-quality data (not checked). Rio Grande (Juárez, Nuevo Laredo, Reynosa), New River (Mexicali) and Santa Cruz (Nogales) depend on it and on IBWC/CILA.

name: Rio Grande / Río Bravo sewage from Ciudad Juárez, Nuevo Laredo, Reynosa, Matamoros
operator: IBWC / CILA, TCEQ, Mexican municipal utilities
status_reason: Shared river with Texas and New Mexico (neither live); IBWC and TCEQ reporting not examined in this round.

name: New River at Calexico (Mexicali sewage into California)
operator: IBWC, Colorado River Basin Regional Water Board
status_reason: Flows north into California's Imperial Valley; reporting not examined in this round.

name: INEGI Red Hidrográfica (Mexico hydrography)
status_reason: Replaces NHD south of the border, with OpenStreetMap as fallback; most affected US reaches start at the boundary, so a border-crossing point may be enough.
